transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I started putting together a memorial for my brother, and it’s grown way beyond what I intended. I’ve been spending most of my days tracking down songs, calling people, planning displays and trips. My wife says I’ve let the garden, my walking group, and pretty much everything else slide.
Have you noticed any change in how much sleep you need to feel rested?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a real change in that.
Have you felt more energetic than usual lately?

Yes, I think so. I can’t seem to sit in my chair the way I used to. I’m up hauling boxes, making calls, rearranging papers, walking from room to room. It feels like I’ve got more steam in me than a man my age ought to have.
Have you felt like your thoughts are racing or moving much faster than usual?

Yes. My mind keeps hopping around—one minute I’m thinking about a display case, then driving somewhere to find a cousin, then a line from a ballad. I can’t seem to slow it down enough to put things in order.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt deeply sad, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy for several weeks?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a stretch like that offhand.
Have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this unusually energetic, active, or full of ideas?

Yes, I’ve had times like this before—where I just can’t stay seated. I’ll be up moving things around, hauling boxes, making phone calls, going from room to room. It feels like I’ve got more energy in my body than I ought to at my age.
Has this increased energy and activity caused severe problems or completely disrupted your everyday life?

Yes, it’s caused problems. I’ve missed my walking group and book club, and I’ve let the garden go. I’ve upset people at the senior center because I keep making everything about the memorial display. My wife says our whole day ends up being about settling me down or steering me away from another call, trip, or argument.
